verdicts.why: I could not find any bound: ValueReader.java:86-89 reads a 32-bit wire length and does `new byte[(int)contentLength]` BEFORE `in.readFully(buffer)`, so no upstream frame-size or TruncatedInputStream limit can prevent the allocation (a 20-byte frame declaring 0x7FFFFFFE still allocates ~2GB); the only inaccuracy is 'or server' in the impact, since this is the Java client library, not the Erlang broker.

The mutual recursion is exactly as described and nothing bounds it: case 'F' at line 181 calls readTable(), which calls readFieldValue() at line 150, and case 'A' at line 184 calls readArray(), which calls readFieldValue() at line 245, with no depth parameter anywhere; each nesting level costs only 5 bytes on the wire ('A' + 4-byte length), so >10,000 levels fit inside a single default 128KB frame.

The quoted code at lines 86-88 is verbatim and the reasoning holds: `contentLength < Integer.MAX_VALUE` only makes the (int) cast safe, and because the array is allocated at line 88 before readFully at line 89, the size is driven purely by the declared length and never by bytes actually available.

The core defect holds (readBytes at lines 86-94 allocates up to Integer.MAX_VALUE-1 bytes from an untrusted length, reachable from readLongstr at line 103 and case 'x' at line 211), but two of its three cited call sites are factually wrong: line 147 is `new TruncatedInputStream(in, tableLength)` and line 241 is readArray's length read, neither of which calls readBytes.

Every cited line checks out (readFieldValue spans 158-221, 'F' at 180-181 -> readTable loop at 150, 'A' at 183-184 -> readArray loop at 245) and no depth counter is threaded through; worse for the defender, each readArray level also stacks a new TruncatedInputStream/DataInputStream whose available() call chain recurses too.

Same unbounded mutual recursion, correctly located: readFieldValue at line 158 reaches itself through readTable (line 181 -> line 150) and readArray (line 184 -> line 245), and there is no guard, depth argument, or caught StackOverflowError in the file to stop it.
